item.title: [7] Spin-density wave of ferrimagnetic building blocks masking the ferromagnetic quantum critical point in NbFe2
item.description:
Last authors: A. Neubauer, C. Pfleiderer, F. M. Grosche, and P. G. Niklowitz

Authors: T. Poulis, G. Mani, J. Sturt, W. J. Duncan, H. Thoma, V. Hutanu, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Neutron diffraction study of modulated magnetic order and quantum criticality in NbFe2.

Tags: #experiment #material #magnetism

Abstract: Ferromagnetic quantum critical points can be masked by emerging modulated magnetic order. Here, the authors use neutron diffraction to show that the example of NbFe 2 provides the first case, where the masking modulated order is a longitudinal spin-density wave. The latter has a large-wavelength incommensurate modulation of its low average moment and is formed from ferrimagnetic building blocks with antiparallel ferromagnetic sheets. The findings can serve as a test case for magnetic quantum order-by-disorder models.

Abstract: Here, the authors establish NaCdCo 2 F 7 as a spin-orbit-entangled J eff =½ pyrochlore antiferromagnet, in which strong geometric frustration and bond disorder drive unconventional spin freezing. Despite the onset of a frozen state, persistent spin dynamics survive to the lowest temperatures, revealing an unusual coexistence of static and dynamic magnetism in a highly frustrated, disordered system.

item.title: [7] Magnetic-field-driven phase switching in the antiferromagnetic Mott insulator Ca3(Ru0.99Ti0.01)2O7
item.description:
Last authors: Bernhard Keimer, Alexander V. Boris

Authors: Ksenia S. Rabinovich, Tim Priessnitz, Nils Gross, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of magnetic transitions in a Mott insulator, relevant to strongly correlated systems.

Tags: #Mottinsulator #magnetism #stronglycorrelated #experimental

Abstract: Isovalent 1% Ti substitution tunes the polar metal Ca 3 Ru 2 O 7 to the edge of its Mott transition. While electronic kinetic energy and strong electron-lattice coupling contribute to the system’s free-energy balance, its magnetic H - T phase diagram is remarkably simple, closely resembling that of a canonical anisotropic antiferromagnet, albeit with substantially renormalized critical fields. Along the easy axis, a first-order spin-flop transition near 6 Tesla reorients the Ru moments while the system remains insulating; a forced-ferromagnetic metal emerges above 10.5 Tesla field.

item.title: [10] Significant modulation of acoustoelectric current associated with charge density wave transitions
item.description:
Last authors: Shintaro Takada, Yasuhiro Niimi

Authors: Natsumi Nikaido, Takuya Kawada, Koji Fujiwara, et al.

Score 10/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct hit: experimental study of CDW transitions in NbSe3 using acoustoelectric current.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #CDW #NbSe3 #2H-TaSe2 #vanderWaals #transport #experimental

Abstract: How collective electronic order responds to strain remains a central question in quantum materials. Here, the authors find that charge density wave (CDW) transitions in NbSe 3 and 2 H -TaSe 2 strongly modulate the acoustoelectric current driven by surface acoustic waves. A simple phenomenological model based on strain-dependent conductivity captures the essential behavior. The work demonstrates acoustoelectric transport as a sensitive probe of CDW physics and opens new avenues for strain-based control of electronic states in van der Waals materials.
